exposure: clinical indications (foetal distress, prior caesarean section, pregnancy-induced hypertension)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1001 women aged 18 to 38, with varying educational backgrounds and occupations, who gave birth at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital.
finding: The study found an overall Caesarean Section (CS) prevalence of 29.31%, with prior caesarean section being a significant predictor, increasing the likelihood of another CS by 50.65%.
mod_finding: CS delivery was associated with longer maternal hospital stays (5.5 vs. 3 days for vaginal births), and educational attainment and affluence significantly influenced women's choice for elective CS.
